entries.topic: Robert Maxwell: publishing empire, Macmillan, the school joint venture, Israel ties, funeral, pension theft

claims.text: Born Jan Ludvik Hoch, 10 June 1923, Slatinske Doly, Czechoslovakia; Military Cross January 1945; Labour MP for Buckingham 1964-70; Pergamon from 1951; 1971 DTI inspectors: not a person who can be relied on to exercise proper stewardship of a publicly quoted company; Mirror Group from Reed for GBP 113m, July 1984; Loftus and Aarons (1997) credit his 1948 Czech contacts and aircraft-parts smuggling; Hersh, Ben-Menashe, Thomas and Dillon allegations; at least six serving and former Israeli intelligence chiefs at the funeral.
Maxwell Communication Corporation paid $2.62 billion for Macmillan Inc., late 1988.

May 1989: McGraw-Hill and Macmillan (a division of Maxwell Communication) formed a 50-50 partnership combining their school units, 1988 revenues $440m, second only to Harcourt Brace Jovanovich in the school market; Maxwell agreed a 15-year standstill on McGraw-Hill stock.

Mount of Olives burial with the pomp of a state funeral; President Herzog delivered the eulogy ('He scaled the heights of human endeavor'); PM Shamir attended; Israeli holdings including Ma'ariv estimated at $300m.
About GBP 460m taken from the pensioners' funds; Kevin and Ian Maxwell tried and acquitted.

entries.topic: Who owns the American school publishers now

claims.text: HMH sale to Veritas Capital completed 7 April 2022, $2.8bn, $21 a share; HMH says it serves more than 50 million students.
Platinum Equity completed its $4.5bn acquisition of McGraw Hill on 2 August 2021.
Pearson sold its US K-12 courseware business to Nexus Capital for $250m (Feb 2019); it became Savvas Learning.

entries.topic: Who decides in America: Texas board, Virginia review, ICS, Newton

claims.text: Texas SBOE: 15 members elected by district (10 R, 5 D, Feb 2026); approves instructional materials and sets TEKS; manages the Permanent School Fund, valued at $60.6bn.

28 Feb 2018 letter from JCRC Richmond, UJF Tidewater and JCRC Greater Washington to the Virginia DOE endorsing ICS reviews of textbooks submitted for adoption; thanks Pearson and McGraw-Hill for earlier changes.

ICS submissions in Virginia, per VCHR: 'settlers' to 'communities', 'occupation' to 'control of', 'wall' to 'security fence', 'militant' to 'terrorist'; 14 Virginia academics urged publishers not to adopt them (30 May 2018).
ICS founded 2005 by JCRC Bay Area; $2.8m national initiative; trained 18,000+ educators in all 50 states; 14,000 'improvements' to materials and standards; independent 501(c)(3) from July 2024.
Six Newton taxpayers sued Newton Public Schools over alleged anti-Israel material; dropped the suit in summer 2019 before any ruling.

Ed Week 2010: Texas one of ~20 adoption states, market second to California; Jay Diskey calls Texas sway 'a bit of an urban myth'; Lee Wilson: big Texas/California book reused as base, not rewritten 'from the ground up'.

entries.topic: Israel's ministry, Germany's KMK, the Palestinian donor model, the Wexler study

claims.text: July 2009: Education Minister Gideon Sa'ar moved to remove 'nakba' from textbooks, undoing Yuli Edelstein's 2007 approval of a sixth-grade text for Arab students.

Knesset, 4-5 Nov 2024, 55-45: Education Ministry director-general may dismiss teachers deemed to back terror; minister may cut school funding. Adalah petition filed 17 Dec 2024; order nisi 31 Dec 2025; pending.
KMK traces to a February 1948 conference in Stuttgart-Hohenheim; permanent from 2 July 1948; decisions by unanimity since the 1949 rules.
December 2000: citing CMIP's study, Italy told the Palestinians it could no longer fund curriculum development; the World Bank diverted textbook and teacher-training funds.

2013 State Department-funded study ($590,000), Wexler, Adwan, Bar-Tal, 94 Palestinian and 74 Israeli books: dehumanizing portrayals rare; 20 extreme negative characterizations in Israeli secular books, 7 ultra-Orthodox, 6 Palestinian; 58% of post-1967 Palestinian maps and 76% of Israeli maps omit the other; Israeli ministry called the comparison unfounded.
European Parliament (May 2025) called for EU funding to the Palestinian Authority to be frozen until textbook reform, pressing the Commission on conditionality agreed the previous year.

claims.text: July 1939: Advertising Federation of America convention resolved to campaign against Rugg's texts; research director Alfred T. Falk said the book was used by 4,200 school systems.

September 1940: Rugg books banned in about half a dozen systems; Bradner, Ohio board vice-president made a bonfire; B.C. Forbes called them subversive; the series had sold about 2 million copies and was used in 4,000 schools.
The AFA and American Legion campaigns; districts pulled the series by the early 1940s.
FitzGerald, America Revised (1979): the adoption process 'all-controlling'; texts' treatment of race changed after the urban uprisings.
Ravitch, The Language Police (2003): bias and sensitivity guidelines; pressure from left and right; publishers' 'preemptive capitulation'.
Ravitch was Assistant Secretary of Education (1991-93).

entries.topic: State laws on antisemitism in schools, 2023-2026

claims.text: Virginia HB 1606 (2023) adopted the IHRA working definition including its Israel examples; Palestine Legal coalition objected.
5 Jan 2026: AG Miyares letter telling K-12 superintendents and boards to adopt IHRA in codes of conduct; incoming governor and AG cannot reverse it without the General Assembly.
AP, Nov 2025: Texas, Arkansas, Oklahoma, Tennessee passed school accountability measures; Arizona governor vetoed one; dozens of states have adopted IHRA; civil liberties groups object.
California AB 715 signed 8 Oct 2025, in force 1 Jan 2026: Office of Civil Rights, Antisemitism Prevention Coordinator, tighter rules on instructional materials.
Aug 2026: Newsom appointed Lele Yutzy to direct the new Office of Civil Rights; the coordinator post not yet filled.
